raw_response:
I don't need to search or compute anything else — I've got 30 years of doing this on my own fields and I've watched my neighbors enough to know what works. Let me think through this season.

My family has four mouths and some of them work off-farm, so I can't be out there all day either. Six mu is not big, but it's what I have and I know every corner of it. I've been wheat-maize for as long as I can remember — wheat goes in around October, comes off in early June, and the maize goes in the same week. There's no time to plough between them; if I tried, I'd miss the planting window and the yield would drop. So wheat gets rotary tilled before planting, and maize gets no-till planted right behind the combine.

For wheat, I use improved seed — I save some but I buy fresh every couple of years to keep the vigor up. I put down compound fertilizer before planting, about 100 jin per mu, and I topdress with urea at jointing because the extension fellow said that helps, though I usually put a little extra on just to be safe — I'd rather waste a few yuan than lose a crop. That works out to roughly 16 kg of nitrogen per mu when you count it all up, plus whatever phosphorus and potassium come in the bag. I irrigate three times: once before winter to help the seedlings settle, once at jointing when the weather turns dry, and once at grain filling. I spray herbicide once after planting, insecticide when I see aphids, and fungicide once because the rust has been bad the last few years. I expect about 480 kg per mu if the spring rain cooperates.

For maize, I buy hybrid seed from the shop — Nongda or Denghai, whatever they have in stock. One package per mu is what everyone does. I put one batch of compound down at planting, about 80 jin per mu, and that's usually enough. I irrigate twice — once right after planting if it's dry, and once at the big trumpet leaf stage. Maize gets herbicide once and insecticide twice because the corn borer always shows up in July. No-till saves me time and diesel. I figure on about 520 kg per mu if the summer storms don't flatten it.

I'm not changing much this year. Last year was decent, prices were alright, and my neighbor who tried some new thing ended up with no better yield than me. At my age, steady is better than clever.
